skill.name: spec-discovery

content.value_statement: Specification requirements are difficult to locate and trace across repositories. This skill extracts requirement IDs, titles, paths, links, and hashes into a sorted manifest.
actual_capabilities: Searches a primary repository and additional local repositories for specification files.
Includes external request specifications and excludes template directories.
Extracts requirement IDs and titles from matching Markdown headings.
Normalizes repository-relative paths and creates lowercase, hyphenated links.
Computes SHA-256 content hashes for traceability.
Sorts results by repository, path, and requirement ID.
limitations: Recognizes only headings with requirement IDs that begin with REQ- and match the documented pattern.
Reads local repository roots and does not clone or fetch remote repositories.
Does not assess requirement quality, completeness, or implementation status.
Flags duplicate requirement IDs but does not resolve them.

use_cases.title: Create a requirement inventory
use_cases.description: Collect requirement IDs, titles, source paths, links, and hashes from a documentation repository.

use_cases.title: Prepare implementation traceability
use_cases.description: Find relevant specifications before coding and retain stable source metadata for reviews.

use_cases.title: Supply downstream agent context
use_cases.description: Produce a compact JSON or TOON manifest for planning, analysis, and documentation workflows.

prompt_templates.title: Scan the current repository
prompt_templates.prompt: Scan the current repository for specifications. Return a JSON manifest with each requirement ID, title, relative path, link, and SHA-256 hash.

prompt_templates.title: Include external requests
prompt_templates.prompt: Scan {root} and include external requests. Exclude templates, preserve ID and title casing, and report duplicate IDs in notes.
prompt_templates.scenario: Focused scan with standard path rules

prompt_templates.title: Scan several repositories
prompt_templates.prompt: Use {primary_root} as ROOT and {additional_roots} as EXTRA_REPOS. Produce a sorted TOON manifest and identify every duplicate requirement ID.

prompt_templates.title: Build an auditable manifest
prompt_templates.prompt: Discover requirements across {repository_roots}. Verify heading matches, normalize links, compute content hashes, and explain skipped files or empty results.

output_examples.output: No specifications were found because the repository has no specs directory. The result is empty and the scan completed normally.

best_practices: Provide explicit repository roots and confirm that each root is available locally.
Use consistent REQ- identifiers and descriptive Markdown heading titles.
Review duplicate IDs and unmatched headings before using the manifest downstream.
anti_patterns: Do not expect requirements in body text to match when they are absent from headings.
Do not treat a content hash as proof that a requirement is correct or approved.
Do not ignore duplicate ID notes when combining several repositories.

faq.question: Which files does this skill inspect?
faq.answer: It inspects specifications under specs/ and optionally specs/external-requests/. It skips specs/templates/.

faq.question: Which requirement IDs are recognized?
faq.answer: It recognizes Markdown headings containing IDs that begin with REQ- and match the documented letters, numbers, underscores, and hyphens pattern.

faq.question: Can it scan more than one repository?
faq.answer: Yes. Set one primary root and provide additional local repository roots through EXTRA_REPOS.

faq.question: What happens when duplicate IDs are found?
faq.answer: The skill keeps the entries and flags the duplicate IDs in manifest notes for review.

faq.question: Does it modify specification files?
faq.answer: No. The workflow reads specification content and produces a separate manifest.

faq.question: Which output formats are supported?
faq.answer: It supports JSON for machine workflows and TOON for compact prompt context.
